paper.title: Optimal Design for Multinomial Logit Model with Applications to Best Assortment Identification

settings.name_in_paper: Best assortment identification (BSI) in MNL bandits with linear utilities
unmapped: Multinomial logit (MNL) choice feedback with outside option: learner offers an assortment of at most m items and observes a single chosen item (or no-purchase), probabilities exp(a_i^T theta)/(1+sum_j exp(a_j^T theta))
Expected revenue objective R(S,theta)=sum_i p(i|S,theta) r_i with known item revenues r_i in [0,1] (non-uniform)
The learner knows the problem-dependent constant kappa = min_S min_{i in S} p(i|S,theta*) p(0|S,theta*) (algorithm input)
Item features a_i in R^d with ||a_i||_2<=1 known; ||theta*||_2 <= B (paper's B = canonical S)
settings.definition_quote: we adopt the MNL choice model with an outside option ... p(i| S,\thetab^\star):=\frac{\exp(\ab_i^\top\thetab^\star)}{1+\sum_{j\in S}\exp(\ab_j^\top\thetab^\star)} ... Let $S^\star\in\argmax_{S \in \Scal}R(S,\thetab^\star)$ denote the optimal assortment and assume the maximizer is unique. Given a failure probability $\delta>0$, our goal is to interact with the environment until a (possibly random) stopping time $\tau$ and return an assortment $\hat S$ such that $\PP(\hat{S} = S^\star \wedge \tau < \infty ) \geq 1-\delta$.

source.label: thm:BSI_MNL
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1)$, $\lambda=1$, and fix the design accuracy $\epsilon\in(0,1]$ with $0\le\ErrorLMO\le\epsilon d/2$. ... Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:MNL_BAI}, when implemented with the MILP solver ..., returns the optimal assortment $S^\star$, and the stopping round $\tau$ satisfies $\tau = \BigOTilde(d \log(N/\delta)(\frac{1}{\Gap^2} + \frac{1}{\kappa\,\Gap}) + \WarmupRounds)$.

results.notes: Paper's N (number of items) mapped to K; paper's K (max assortment size) mapped to m; paper's Delta (minimum revenue gap between best and second-best assortment) mapped to Delta_min. Also restated as non-uniform case of Theorem C.1. Total observations at most 2*tau. MILP LMO is NP-hard in general, so compute not_stated.

source.quote: Under the setting as in Theorem~\ref{thm:BSI_MNL}, suppose we employ the lifted G-optimal design ... Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $\tau = \BigOTilde( (1+ \ErrorLift) d \log(N/\delta) ( \frac{1}{\Gap^2} + \frac{1}{\kappa\,\Gap} ) + \WarmupRounds )$

source.label: lemma:exploration_phase_length
source.quote: There is an absolute constant $c_0>0$ such that \WarmupRounds\le c_0\kappa^{-1}d \left(d\log\frac{16(N+1)^2}{\delta}\vee B^2\right) \log\!\left(1+\frac{K}{\kappa} \left[d\log\frac{16(N+1)^2}{\delta}\vee B^2\right]\right). Moreover, $\PP(\Ecal)\ge1-\delta/2$.

results.notes: Bound on number of warm-up rounds T_0 (deterministic bound from the elliptical potential argument; the probability statement concerns the confidence event). Quantity 'other' since it bounds only the warm-up phase length.
